title: Grape Dumplings
description: Have you ever heard of Grape Dumplings? Here’s your chance to try this North Carolina treat by following this kidney-friendly recipe from DaVita dietitian Barb.
steps: In a medium bowl combine flour, baking powder, sugar, salt and shortening. Add 1/2-cup grape juice and mix into a stiff dough.
Roll dough very thin on a floured board and cut into strips 1/2” wide and 1” long.
Mix 1-cup grape juice with 1-cup water in a saucepan and heat to a boil.
Drop dough pieces into boiling grape juice and cook for 10 to 12 minutes.
Serve dumpling with small amount of liquid.
hints: Serve as a side dish with your meal or for dessert.

title: Macaroni and Cheese
description: Macaroni and Cheese is the ultimate comfort food. Michele from North Carolina created this lower phosphorus, lower sodium version to satify her family while keeping it renal friendly.
ingredients: 1 cup whole wheat rotini pasta, uncooked
steps: Cook pasta according to box instructions, omitting salt.

In a saucepan on low heat, melt butter. Add garlic and simmer for one minute. Add cream cheese and stir until melted. Add 1/2 cup milk and whisk to make a sauce. Add more milk to desired consistency. Simmer sauce on low-medium heat, being careful not to burn.
Stir in the parmesan cheese. Add a few sprinkles of the red pepper flakes and black pepper to taste.
Mix sauce with the cooked pasta and enjoy!
hints: Vegetables and cooked chicken can also be added if desired to make a one-dish meal.

title: Strawberry Sorbet
description: It’s time to cool off during these warm months, so why not induldge in a healthy way with the kidney-friendly recipe for Strawberry Sorbet.
steps: Place ice in blender
Add all ingredients
Turn speed to crush or liquefy
hints: May be prepared in ice tray or Popsicle® holders.
Add sugar or sugar substitute for extra sweetness.

title: Cranberry Cabbage
description: DaVita dietitian, Heather from Georgia, enjoys spending time in the kitchen coming up with delicious kidney-friendly recipes for her patients to enjoy. One of her favorites is Cranberry Cabbage.
steps: In large pan heat cranberry sauce, lemon juice and cloves together and bring to a simmer.
Stir cabbage into melted cranberry sauce, mixing well. Bring mixture to a boil; reduce heat to simmer. Continue cooking until cabbage is tender, stirring occasionally.
Serve hot.
hints: One medium head of cabbage yields 6 cups chopped.

title: Apple Cinnamon Flavored Water
description: Water is one of the healthiest beverages for kidney patients–but nobody says it has to be plain and tasteless! Try Apple-Cinnamon Flavored Water, one of many flavored water recipes from DaVita dietitian Kara.
steps: Cut unpeeled apple into thin slices.
Add all ingredients to a pitcher.
Refrigerator overnight before serving.
hints: If you are on limited fluids, adjust the portion size to meet your needs.
After flavors develop you can pour into ice cube trays to make flavored ice.

title: Tuna Salad with Apple and Celery
description: Matilde, a DaVita dietitian from Texas, understands food represents comfort and adopting a healthy diet can be difficult for her patients. That’s why one of Matilde’s many talents is sharing family favorite recipes that are tasty and kidney-friendly. This tuna salad with apple and celery is savory, rich in protein and easy to prepare.
serving_size: 1/4 of the bowl of tuna (approximately 3/4 cup)
ingredients: 15 ounces canned unsalted tuna, packed in water
steps: Drain tuna and finely chop apple, celery and onion.
Mix tuna, apple, celery, onion, mayonnaise, black pepper and salt in a medium bowl.
Serve on top of bed of lettuce, with unsalted crackers or make a sandwich.
hints: Adjust portion if you are on a lower protein diet. Ask your dietitian to recommend the correct portion for your individual needs.
The juices from the fruit and vegetables will maintain moisture in the tuna salad.
If you’d like to munch something crunchy, try Matilde’s Tuna Salad with celery sticks or lightly steamed green beans.
Sodium is 121 mg per serving if salt is omitted.

title: Cranberry Oatmeal Breakfast Cookies
description: Grab a cookie for breakfast–only if it contains healthy ingredients like those found in kidney-friendly Cranberry Oatmeal Breakfast Cookies. Applesauce, cranberries, oatmeal and protein powder transform these flavor-packed cookies into a great breakfast choice.
steps: Set butter out to soften to room temperature. Preheat oven to 350° F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Using an electric mixer, cream together butter and sugar. Add in the egg, flour, protein powder, vanilla extract, cinnamon and salt. Stir to combine.
Add in the applesauce and combine. Fold in the oats and cranberries.
Scoop 1/4 cup scoops of the cookie dough onto the baking sheet. Flatten each cookie slightly.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until cookies are golden brown but still soft.
Allow cookies to cool for 5 minutes on the baking sheet before transferring to a rack to cool completely.
hints: Store cookies in an air tight container or wrap individually and freeze until ready to grab for a quick breakfast on the go.
Scoop sizes vary for different protein powder brands. Check the label to see weight of one scoop to determine how much to add or use a scale to measure 1.5 ounces.
Enjoy breakfast cookies as a snack. Consider making 24 smaller cookies instead of 12.

title: Horseradish Marinade Flank Steak
description: This marinade helps keep this steak tender and juicy while providing a lot of flavor.
steps: Pierce the flank steak with a fork so that the steak can soak up the flavors of the marinade. Lightly pepper both sides.

Crush and mince the garlic. Whisk the oil, garlic, horseradish and mustard together in a covered container or disposable bag. Coat the steak and massage in marinade. Let stand in the refrigerator for at least 2-4 hours or for best results overnight.

Grill steak for around 5 minutes per side to desired doneness and when internal temperature has reached 165 degrees. Remove the steak from the grill to a clean cutting board and allow to rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. Alternatively you may use a grill pan or skillet on the stove top.
hints: Look for steak that is pre-cut and thin. If it is not thin you may cover with plastic wrap and pound flat. This helps the steak cook quicker and more evenly.
Look for horseradish and coarse mustard with the lowest amount of sodium per serving.

title: Chicken Lemon Rice Soup
description: This chicken and rice soup has a hit of lemon, which gives a unique flavor to this soup.
steps: Chop onion, celery and chicken. Mince garlic and slice the carrot. Heat a 5-quart saucepan over medium heat. Add in olive oil, onion, celery, garlic, and carrot. Sauté about 5 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Add in the chicken and 4 cups of the water, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and rice. Cook 15 minutes over medium heat or until rice is done.
Add last 4 cups of water and continue cooking until heated through.
hints: Cutting salt back to 1/4 teaspoon will bring the sodium down to 211 mg per serving.

You may use brown or white rice in this recipe. The brown rice may take a little longer to soften. The brown rice has slightly more potassium and phosphorus, but not all of those minerals will be absorbed by the body.

title: Calabrian Chicken
description: This chicken brings a bit of warmth and sweet. Try it in place of how you would typically prepare chicken.
steps: Juice the lemon. In a small bowl, combine lemon juice, Calabrian chili paste, and honey. Stir to combine.
Slice each chicken breast in half so that you are left with 2 thin cutlets. Season with pepper on each side.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add chicken to pan and cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees.
Once chicken is done, mince garlic and add to the pan and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add chili mixture and heavy cream and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes.
Plate chicken and pour remaining sauce over chicken.
Serve with rice as an option and enjoy! (rice is not accounted for in nutrients per serving).
hints: Calabrian chili paste can be spicy. If you are sensitive to spicy food, you can reduce the amount of chili paste by half.
If unable to find Calabrian chili paste, it can be substituted with chopped Calabrian chilis, a thicker chili sauce, or red pepper flakes.

title: Easy Honey Mustard Balsamic Vinaigrette
description: The next time you’re whipping up a salad, consider topping it with Wai Yin’s Easy Honey Mustard Balsamic Vinaigrette. A mix of kidney-friendly ingredients–balsamic vinegar, olive oil, mustard, honey and black pepper, it has a sweet and spicy flavor that makes any salad a standout.
steps: Put all ingredients in a jar. Cover and shake vigorously,then serve immediately.
If dressing is prepared ahead of time, shake well before serving.
hints: Drizzle on top of salad greens, or put in a small serving dish for dipping (to prevent overuse of dressing).
Store leftover dressing in the refrigerator for up to one week.
Compare brands and select the lowest sodium mustard.

title: Swedish Meatballs
description: This recipe for Swedish Meatballs was made with the kidney diet in mind. This yummy dish can be made with reduced sodium and can also be made in advance.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Chop onion. Beat eggs.
Combine first 11 ingredients in a large bowl and mix well.
Roll into 1” balls and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until meatballs are cooked through.
To make sauce, melt butter in a large saucepan.
Add flour, reduced-sodium broth, remaining tablespoon dried thyme and water.Cook over medium heat, stirring until thickened.
Add meatballs to sauce and lower temperature to keep warm or place in a covered warming dish or slow cooker on low heat setting.
hints: Reduced-sodium broth contains 450 to 500 mg sodium per cup. Low-sodium broth contains 140 mg sodium or less per cup.
Make meatballs ahead and refrigerate. When ready to serve, heat ingredients together and transfer to a warming dish.

title: Low Sugar Carrot Cake
description: For people on dialysis cooking your own foods and baking your own desserts helps you control your dialysis diet. Try this recipe for Low Sugar Carrot Cake and bake up a delicious after-dinner dessert or mid-day snack that is sure to be a hit.
ingredients: 1 cup Splenda® Sugar Blend for Baking
3/4 cup Splenda® No Calorie Sweetener, granulated
steps: Preheat oven to 350o F.
Grease and lightly flour a 9″ x 13″ pan.
Sift flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder and cinnamon together. Set aside.
Combine oil and Splenda® Sugar Blend for Baking. Add in one egg at a time, mixing after each egg is added.
Gradually add dry ingredients. Mix well.
Fold in shredded carrots. Pour into baking pan and bake for 55 to 60 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
To make icing, combine butter and cream cheese in a mixing bowl. Beat with a mixer until light and fluffy.
Gradually add Splenda® granulated sweetener while beating. Add vanilla and mix well.
Spread icing on cake after it cools well.
hints: For a lower fat version, replace 1/2-cup canola oil with 1/2-cup unsweetened applesauce; replace eggs with 1-cup low-cholesterol egg product; use reduced-calorie cream cheese. (250 calories, 18 grams fat per serving).
If desired, replace Splenda products with equal amounts of sugar.

Splenda is available in four forms: Splenda® Sugar Blend for Baking (half Splenda®, half sugar), Splenda® Brown sugar Blend (half Splenda, half brown sugar), Splenda® granulater sweetener and Splenda® tabletop sweetener. For best results use the two types specified in this recipe.

title: Puerto Rican Style Chicken Skewers
description: Chicken barbecued on skewers and seasoned with Adobo seasoning and guava barbecue sauce is sure to please everyone at the table.
ingredients: 1 cup Guava BBQ Sauce (see DaVita.com recipe)
steps: Dice chicken thighs into 2-inch bite-sized pieces. If using bamboos skewers, soak in water for 1/2 hour to prevent burning.
Mix together the Adobo Seasoning, oregano, vinegar, olive oil and bay leaves and put in a zip top bag.
Add chicken to the marinade. Place in the refrigerator to for at least a half hour to overnight.
Heat the grill and oil the grates when hot.
Thread the chicken on skewers and place on the hot grill. Sear for about 5 minutes on each side.
Baste the pinchos with Guava Barbecue Sauce or other low sodium barbecue sauce and cook for about 4 more minutes.
hints: Keep the chicken pieces about the same size to ensure even cooking.
Check out our Guava Barbecue Sauce and additional low-sodium barbecue sauce recipes on DaVita.com.
Make your own lower sodium Adobe Seasoning.

title: Spicy Beef Stew
description: Spicy Beef Stew has a unique taste from the red pepper, curry powder and peanut butter. This soup is low in both sodium and phosphorus yet high in flavor.
steps: Dice the onion and tomato. Peel and chop the carrots. Cut stew meat into cubes.
In a large pan, heat oil until hot. Add the beef and cook and stir over medium heat until browned.
Add the onion to the meat and sauté until clear, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the water, tomato paste, red and black peppers and curry powder. Cover pan and cook over medium-low heat until vegetables are tender, 20 to 25 minutes.
Add the peanut butter and stir to combine. Cover and cook over low heat for an additional 20 minutes.
Serve over hot rice.
hints: Adjust the red pepper to taste.
Refrigerate or freeze leftover stew.

title: Lucky Shamrock Creamy Pineapple Dessert
description: Lucky Shamrock Creamy Pineapple Dessert was created by DaVita renal dietitian Judy as a way for her dialysis patients to get extra protein in a tasty dessert.
ingredients: 15 ounces crushed pineapple canned in juice
steps: Thaw whipped topping.
Drain the juice from crushed pineapple.
In a medium bowl mix the cottage cheese and crushed pineapple together.
Gently fold in the whipped topping and green food coloring until mixed well.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: To serve as a festive Saint Patrick’s Day dessert, garnish the top with a dash of green sprinkles or colored sugar.
For other holidays change the food coloring and garnish colors.
This is a tasty way to boost high quality protein intake.

title: Country Soda Biscuits
description: Country Soda Biscuits are a breakfast staple in the southern part of the US. DaVita dietitians from North Carolina share this tasty biscuit recipe for everyone to enjoy. They have modified the recipe by replacing higher phosphorus items with those lower in phosphorus. This is to help dialysis patients enjoy this southern specialty and stay within their phosphorus limits.
steps: Preheat oven to 475° F.
Stir baking soda into buttermilk.
Combine flour and salt in a bowl. Cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Sprinkle buttermilk over flour mixture and stir until dry ingredients are moistened and dough is formed.
Knead dough on a floured surface 6 times. Roll dough out to 1/2” thickness. Using a 2” biscuit cutter, cut out 12 biscuits.
Bake on a greased baking sheet for 10 to 12 minutes, until browned.
hints: Biscuits leavened with baking soda and buttermilk are lower in phosphorus compared to baking powder biscuits.
One biscuit served with 1/3-cup Country Gravy provides 198 mg sodium and 98 mg phosphorus. Be aware that portion size can make a difference in how much sodium and phosphorus are consumed.

title: Reduced-Fat Low-Sodium Mayonnaise Spread
description: Expand your culinary repertoire with new idea for a topping. DaVita dietitian,Lynn from Maryland,says you can make any meal better with her kidney-friendly recipe for Reduced-Fat Low-Sodium Mayonnaise Spread.
steps: Combine ingredients in a small bowl.
Use as desired.
hints: Mix with salad ingredients or as a sandwich spread.
Heat and use as a cream sauce on vegetables.
Substitute low fat mayonnaise for even lower fat content.

title: Chicken and Rice Casserole
description: Trying to put together a nutritious, delicious and kidney-friendly meal can be challenging. So the DaVita renal dietitian team offers a little assistance with a recipe recommended for the kidney diet, Chicken and Rice Casserole.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Heat oven to 350° F. Spray a 1-1/2-quart baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Chop bell pepper and onion.
In a large saucepan, heat olive oil and butter over low heat.
After butter is melted, stir in flour and black pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly. Remove from heat.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce, broth and milk. Heat to a boil, stirring constantly. Boil and stir for one minute.
Stir in cooked rice, chicken, mushrooms, bell pepper, onion and Mrs. Dash herb seasoning.
Pour into baking dish. Cover and bake for 30 minutes. Remove cover and continue cooking for 20 minutes.
hints: Portion leftovers and freeze to reheat later for a quick meal.
For variation, substitute 2 cups frozen mixed vegetables for bell peppers and mushrooms.
Reduce or increase the amount of poultry for a lower or higher protein meal.
Substitute turkey for chicken if desired.

title: Ratatouille
description: This tasty all-vegetable Ratatouille delivers big flavor in well-under an hour. Use heart-healthy canola or olive oil in the skillet to add calories and healthy fats. Ratatouille is a great fit for kidney patients who need to include some higher potassium foods in their diet.
steps: Dice onion, squash, eggplant, carrots and peppers. Mince garlic cloves. Add canola or olive oil to large skillet, with garlic, herbs, black pepper and carrots.
Cook 2 minutes, then add the rest of the vegetables, except tomatoes.
Sauté well and stir frequently, 10–15 minutes or until vegetables are semi-tender.
Add tomatoes and parmesan cheese and mix well.
Simmer covered for approximately 1/2 hour.
hints: If using dried herbs instead of fresh, decrease to 1 teaspoon each instead of 1 tablespoon.
Substitute an Italian herb blend for separate herbs, if desired.
If you are on a low potassium diet count as 1-1/2 vegetable servings.
Prepare Ratatouille as a side dish or add pasta (small shells, bow ties or elbows) or make it a complete meal by adding cooked ground turkey, chicken or beef.
Freeze extra portions for a quick dish later.

title: Quick and Easy Ground Beef Soup
description: Your next kidney-friendly meal is only four easy steps away with Quick and Easy Ground Beef Soup. This combination of mixed vegetables, beef and rice is tasty and filling and a definite keeper for the quick meal file.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Mrs. Dash® lemon pepper seasoning blend
1 teaspoon Kitchen Bouquet® seasoning and browning sauce
3 cups frozen mixed vegetables (corn, green beans, peas and carrots)
steps: Chop onion. In a large saucepan, brown ground beef with onion. Drain fat.
Add seasoning and browning sauce, broth, water, rice and mixed vegetables.
Bring to a boil on high heat. Reduce to medium-low heat, cover and cook 30 minutes.
Remove from heat, stir in sour cream and serve.
Optional preparation method:
Mix uncooked ground beef, chopped onion, Mrs. Dash and Kitchen Bouquet together in a bowl. Roll into walnut-size meat balls.
In a large saucepan combine broth, water, rice and mixed vegetables. Bring to a boil on high heat.
Drop meatballs into the boiling broth, reduce to medium-low heat and cook for 30 minutes or until meatballs are cooked through.
hints: Look for reduced-sodium broth containing 500 milligrams sodium or less per 1 cup serving. Avoid low-sodium broth that contains potassium chloride—it is very high in potassium.
Optional vegetable mixture includes cauliflower, carrots and snow peas (reduces phosphorus to 190 milligrams per serving.)

title: Royal Meringue Cookies
description: They say a good cook loves food and people equally. That’s certainly the case for Barbara from Alabama who says she was drawn to be a dietitian because it was a great combination of the two. Barbara’s Royal Meringue Cookies are light-as-air treats that literally melt in your mouth. Made with love, there’s almost nothing better than these kidney-friendly cookies.
steps: Preheat oven to 275° F.
Lightly butter and flour two large cookie sheets.
In a large bowl, let the egg whites warm to room temperature, about 15 minutes.
With electric mixer at high speed, beat egg whites with cream of tartar, salt and vanilla until soft peaks form when beater is slowly raised.
Gradually beat in granulated sugar two teaspoons at a time, until very stiff peaks form. Mixture should be moist and shiny.
Drop meringue by tablespoonfuls, using rubber spatula to push meringue from spoon to form mounds, 1” apart. There should be approximately 40 mounds.
Sprinkle each mound with sprinkles if desired.
Bake about 1 hour or until crisp and very light golden color.
Open oven door and let meringues cool for 1 hour before removing from cookie sheet. Store in a covered container until ready to serve.
hints: Add an extract such as lemon or almond for extra flavoring.

title: Popcorn Brittle
description: Popcorn Brittle is a creation from DaVita dietitian Mary to give her patients a substitute for peanut brittle. Popcorn instead of peanuts means lower potassium and phosphorus content.
ingredients: 5-1/2 cups popcorn, air-popped without salt or fat
steps: Line a baking sheet with foil; coat foil with cooking spray. Set aside.
Place popped popcorn in a large, zip-top plastic bag; seal. Crush popcorn using a meat mallet or rolling pin; set aside.

Combine sugar, syrup and 1/4 cup water in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook 1 minute or until sugar dissolves, stirring constantly. Cook, without stirring, until a candy thermometer registers 270° F (about 8 minutes).
Stir in molasses and butter. Cook until thermometer registers 290° F (about 5 minutes).
Stir in baking soda, vanilla and salt.
Stir crushed popcorn into boiling syrup mixture and remove from heat.
Working quickly, pour popcorn mixture onto prepared pan. Spread to 1/4″ thickness using a wooden spoon coated with cooking spray.
Cool completely; break into large pieces.
hints: Store brittle in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days.
Not recommended for people with diabetes due to high sugar content.

title: Chicken Enchiladas with Green Sauce
description: Shredded chicken and cheese rolled in flour tortillas topped with salsa verde and sour cream are the ingredients in these delicious Chicken Enchiladas with Green Sauce.
steps: Prepare Salsa Verde and Flour Tortillas recipes.
In a large pot, place chicken breast, broth and garlic cloves. Poach chicken for 30 minutes on medium-low heat.
Remove chicken from pot and in a separate container shred chicken using 2 forks. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 350° F. Spray a baking dish with cooking spray.
Place Salsa Verde in a shallow frying pan and heat on low heat.
In a separate pan, heat tortillas and transfer into the frying pan. Drench tortillas in salsa one by one; set aside
Once all tortillas have been drenched, start assembling the enchiladas by stuffing with chicken and cheese and rolling them so that the seam side is down in the baking dish. (Divide the
chicken and cheese equally between the 6 tortillas.) Pour the remaining Salsa Verde over top of enchiladas. Cover dish with foil and heat in the oven for 15 minutes.
Top each enchilada with 1 tablespoon sour cream. Enjoy!
hints: For added flavor top enchiladas with chopped onions or cilantro.
Commercially prepared salsa verde and flour tortillas may be substituted, but sodium will be higher. Look for the lowest sodium brands.
Most flour tortillas are high in sodium. Lower sodium brands include Tortilla Land® Fresh Ready-to-Cook Tortillas (210 mg sodium), La Banderita® Low Sodium Tortillas (85 mg sodium).

title: Holiday Tuna Ball
description: Holiday Tuna Ball is a great substitute for the traditional holiday cheese ball. The low sodium, potassium and phosphorus content makes this the perfect addition to your holiday appetizer list.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften for 30 minutes.
Drain canned tuna and flake with a fork.
In a mixing bowl combine cream cheese, tuna, cranberries, celery, onion and cumin. Mix with an electric mixer until well combined.
Combine the bread crumbs and parsley then place on a plate. Shape the cream cheese mixture into a ball and roll in bread crumbs to cover.
Wrap the ball in plastic wrap and refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: Serve with low-sodium crackers, apple slices or raw veggies.

title: Honey Mint Fruit Salad
description: Low potassium fruits are complimented with a taste of honey and mint in this healthy, easy to make Honey Mint Fruit Salad.
steps: Wash and dry fresh fruit. Peel the peach and core the unpeeled apple and dice into bite-size pieces. Slice the strawberries. Chop the mint.
In a large bowl combine the fruit.
Drizzle honey over fruit and add the mint. Stir to combine.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: If fresh peach and blueberries are not in season use frozen. Thaw before making fruit salad.
This salad keeps for up to 1 week in the refrigerator.

title: Cauliflower Manchurian
description: Cauliflower Manchurian is a popular Indian-Chinese dish. DaVita renal dietitian shares her kidney-friendly version. with lower sodium content.
steps: Separate cauliflower into florets. Finely shred ginger root and mince garlic clove.
Steam cauliflower in microwave for 12 minutes on medium setting, until soft but not mushy.
Combine ginger root, garlic, spices and rice flour. Coat cauliflower uniformly.
Heat oil. Deep fry coated cauliflower florets in hot oil until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Drizzle with lemon juice and serve hot.
hints: Adjust chili powder for more or less heat.

title: Percolator Punch
description: Kick off the warm months of the year with this kidney-friendly recipe for Percolator Punch.
steps: Pour juices and water into a coffee percolator.
Place remaining ingredients in the percolator basket.
Perk just like regular coffee, until perking stops. Serve warm.
hints: No percolator? No problem. Use a saucepan to heat ingredients to a boil then simmer for 20 minutes.

title: Grilled Peanut Butter and Jelly Sandwich
description: Everyone loves peanut butter and jelly, and now DaVita renal dietitian Shannon from Florida shares her kidney-friendly recipe for a new twist on an old favorite. This easy-to-make sandwich is grilled so that the outside becomes nice and crispy while the inside melts into a gooey, delicious filling.
steps: Spread the peanut butter and jelly on the bread, and place bread together. Butter the outside of the bread.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat. Grill the sandwich until lightly browned on both sides.
hints: If preferred use margarine instead of butter.
Any flavor jelly is acceptable.Serve with carrot sticks and apple slices.
Select low-sodium peanut butter to reduce sodium to 350 mg.
Peanut butter is a high potassium, high phosphorus ingredient but still works in a kidney diet as a substitute for meat. Portion control is important.
Additional phosphate binder may be required if eaten as a snack—check with your renal dietitian.

title: Watermelon-Rosemary Flavored Water
description: Water is one of the healthiest beverages for kidney patients–but nobody says it has to be plain and tasteless! Try Watermelon-Rosemary Flavored Water, one of many flavored water recipes from DaVita dietitian Kara.
steps: Cut watermelon into cubes.
Add all ingredients to a pitcher.
Refrigerate overnight before serving.
hints: If you are on limited fluids, adjust the portion size to meet your needs.
After flavors develop you can pour into ice cube trays to make flavored ice.

title: Tortilla Beef Rollup Lunch Box
description: DaVita dietitian Sara’s Tortilla Beef Rollup Lunch Box is a quick way to make a meal for home or on the go. This kidney-friendly recipe is a blend of sliced roast beef, red onion, bell pepper, cucumber, lettuce and cream cheese, all wrapped up in a flour tortilla. The grapes and almonds boost the fiber and make this a complete meal.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash herb seasoning blend
steps: Slice the roast beef and cucumber; chop the onion and bell pepper. Remove rib from romaine lettuce leaf.
To prepare the beef rollup, spread cream cheese on the tortilla. Layer roast beef slices and vegetables on top. Sprinkle with herb seasoning.
Roll tortilla up like a jelly roll and cut into 4 pieces.
Place rollup, grapes and almonds on a plate or in divided lunch container.
hints: Beverage suggestions: lemonade, flavored sparkling water, lemon-lime soda, fresh brewed tea or coffee.
For an on-the-go meal pack a lunch box with an ice pack to keep food cool until ready to eat.

title: Meat and Rice Balls
description: Meat and Rice Balls isn’t the original name of this tasty kidney-friendly recipe. These beef and rice meatballs were nicknamed Porcupine Balls because the rice sticks up like quills, just like a porcupine. The recipe is from DaVita renal dietitian, Ken from Missouri, and it’s an old family favorite that’s been tried and tested over the years.
ingredients: 3/4 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: In a large bowl, mix ground beef, egg and rice.
After thoroughly mixed, roll into 24 small balls.
Brown balls in skillet on all sides.
Mix the Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning with the water.
Carefully pour the water and Mrs. Dash mixture in the skillet with the meatballs.
Bring water to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, rotating balls on all sides.
hints: For a lower fat dish, replace ground beef with ground turkey.
If you are on a lower protein diet, adjust the portion to match your meal plan.

title: Cheesy Grits
description: The extra flavor in sharp cheese makes this dish cheesy but still kidney-friendly. Try Cheesy Grits with eggs for breakfast or with shrimp for dinner.
steps: In a medium pan, heat water, milk and salt over medium-high heat until boiling.
Add grits and stir. Decrease heat to low and partially cover pan with a lid. For smooth grits, stir often.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes for old-fashioned grits, or 8 to 9 minutes for quick-cooking grits.
Remove pan from heat and stir in butter.
Divide into 2 portions and top each serving with 2 tablespoons shredded cheese. Stir in the cheese and serve hot.
hints: Sharp or extra sharp cheddar cheese results in a cheesier flavor while using a limited amount. For additional cheesier taste and B vitamins boost, stir in 1 to 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Increase dry grits to 1/2 cup for thicker grits.
Avoid instant grits. Sodium ranges from 340 to 520 mg per serving.
Unsweetened milk alternatives like almond, rice or soy milk can be used instead of cow’s milk.

title: Buffalo Chicken Dip
description: Buffalo Chicken has all the flavor of hot and spicy Buffalo wings in a smooth and luscious dip loaded with cream cheese and sour cream. And because this dip’s kidney-friendly, all of your family, friends and coworkers can enjoy it.
steps: Set the cream cheese out to soften.
Drain the red peppers and measure 1/2 cup. Puree in a blender or food processor to make red pepper sauce.
In a medium bowl mix cream cheese and sour cream together until smooth. Add pureed peppers and 2 teaspoons of Tabasco sauce. Stir until combined.
Add the chicken and gently mix. Add additional hot sauce 1/2 teaspoon at a time; taste and continue to add hot sauce to the heat level you desire.
Place mixture in a slow cooker for 2 to 3 hours on low heat, or bake in the oven at 350° F for 30 minutes.
Serve warm dip with carrots, celery, cucumber, cauliflower for dipping, or make mini roll-ups by wrapping dip inside lettuce or cabbage leaves.
hints: Look for bottled or canned roasted red peppers with 85 mg or less sodium per ounce, or roast fresh red peppers to puree. Trader Joe’s fire roasted red peppers contain only 60 mg sodium per ounce.
May also use frozen roasted red peppers if available.
Hot sauce brands and varieties vary greatly in sodium content. Stick to the original Tabasco® hot pepper sauce because it’s much lower in sodium. Increase to 6 teaspoons if you like more heat.
Serve with raw vegetables. Lower potassium choices include carrots, celery, cucumber, cauliflower for dipping, or lettuce or cabbage leaves for wraps.
If serving at a party bake then place in a small slow cooker to keep warm.

title: Homemade Chicken and Dumplings (or Turkey)
description: Today,in our world of fast and convenience foods,we can forget that simple foods made with basic ingredients are usually more delicious and satisfying. Donna,a DaVita renal dietitian from Texas,shares her down home recipe for Homemade Chicken and Dumplings and invites you to add this meal to your healthy renal diet. Here’s a recipe you can follow for a dish that will be scrumptious and keep you successful on your dialysis diet.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
3 cups potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4” thick
steps: Peel and slice potatoes. Soak in a lage pot of water for 3-4 hours to remove some of the potassium, or boil potatoes for 5 minutes, drain water, then add fresh water and cook until tender.Place chicken or turkey pieces in Dutch oven with 6 cups water. Add celery, salt, pepper and herb seasoning. Bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer, covered for 60 minutes or until tender. Remove meat from bones and set aside.
Add leached or double-boiled potatoes and onion to broth. Bring broth to a boil and cook until potatoes are tender, approximately 15 minutes. Remove vegetables with slotted spoon and set aside.
In a large bowl, mix flour and butter together with a fork. Add egg and 2 tablespoons water; mix with fork until ingredients are moistened.
Roll out dough 1/3” thick. With a sharp knife, cut dough into strips.
Add noodle strips to broth and cook for 15 minutes (If using prepackaged dumpling noodles, simply add them to the broth at this time.)
Add vegetables and meat to the broth and simmer for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve.
hints: For convenience, you can use a package of prepared dumpling noodles like Mary B’s® brand, which can be found in the frozen food section of your grocery store.
If you are on a protein-modified diet, select a smaller 2.5-pound chicken to reduce protein to 21 grams per serving.
Substitute 3 turkey legs, skinned, boned and chopped for chicken.

title: Teriyaki Tempeh Vegetable Bowl
description: Tempeh is fermented soy beans. It is generally low in sodium and a great source of protein. You can get creative by using it cubed, sliced, crumbled and added to your favorite dish in place of meat.
serving_size: 1/3 cup rice, 2 ounces tempeh, 1/4 of the veggies
steps: Slice tempeh into 12 crosswise short strips. Heat olive oil in a pan and add tempeh. Cook and flip for 8-10 minutes until it starts to turn brown.
Cook rice according to package directions, see Helpful Hints.

In a small saucepan whisk together coconut amino, 1/4 cup water, honey and rice vinegar, bring to a boil. Meanwhile combine cornstarch and 4 teaspoons water. Add to the boiling sauce and whisk until is starts to thicken.
Pour the sauce over the tempeh in the saucepan and heat through for 5-8 minutes.
Steam/cook the broccoli in the microwave. Drain if needed and set aside.

Divide rice into 4 bowls, about 1/3 cup per bowl. Add broccoli (1/2 cup) to each bowl and place 3 slices of tempeh on top. Drizzle each bowl with 2 tablespoons of crema. Slice scallion and sprinkle over each of the bowls, if desired.
hints: Used instant brown rice. Used 1-1/3 cups water to cook, bring to a boil and then simmer covered for 10 minutes.
The steamer vegetable bag at 12.6 ounces yields about 2 cups of vegetables.
Tempeh is naturally low in sodium. However, when comparing brands, be sure to choose the lowest sodium brand. If it is not marinated the sodium content should be very low.
A crema dressing can be added as an option. Stir together 4 tablespoons of sour cream with 3 tablespoons of water. This will add 15 mg potassium and 9mg of phosphorus per serving.

title: Raspberry-Lime Flavored Water
description: Water is one of the healthiest beverages for kidney patients–but nobody says it has to be plain and tasteless! Try Raspberry-Lime Flavored Water, one of many flavored water recipes from DaVita dietitian Kara.
steps: Thinly slice lime.
Finely chop mint leaves.
Add all ingredients to a pitcher.
Refrigerator overnight before serving.
hints: Add a few berries to each cup of flavored water.
For variety try strawberries instead of raspberries.
If you are on limited fluids, adjust the portion size to meet your needs.
After flavors develop you can pour into ice cube trays to make flavored ice.

title: Middle Eastern Seasoning Blend
description: Make this Middle Eastern seasoning blend for your meat, poultry, or rice to add flavor without added salt.
steps: Place ingredients in a jar and shake to combine.
Store until ready to use.
hints: Use to season meat, poultry or rice.
Adjust the amount to suit your taste.

title: Pasta Primavera
description: Pasta Primavera is a perfect kidney-friendly recipe to make for a large group.
steps: Cook pasta and vegetables in separate pots according to package directions, but omitting salt. Drain.
Pour low-sodium chicken broth in a medium-sized stockpot and heat on low heat.
Add flour to broth whisking vigorously to avoid clumps from forming.
Add half and half and garlic powder and stir.
Simmer on low heat for 5 to 10 minutes until mixture thickens slightly. Stir occasionally while simmering.
Add cooked vegetables and pasta. Cook until heated through.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and serve.
hints: Frozen vegetable mixtures vary in potassium content. Choose a mixture with lower potassium vegetables or ask your dietitian to recommend the best choices for your diet if you are limiting potassium.
12 ounces uncooked pasta equals approximately 6 cups cooked pasta.

title: Zucchini Pancakes
description: Zucchini Pancakes are a creative and quick way for people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) to eat their vegetables. With its hash brown-like consistency, this recipe consists of yummy zucchini slices, savory onion and eggs that keep it all together. Enjoy this vegetable dish with a tablespoon of applesauce or cranberry sauce. It’s sure to become a favorite!
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® original blend herb seasoning
1/4 cup liquid low cholesterol egg substitute
steps: Grate onion and zucchini into a bowl and stir to combine. Place the zucchini mixture on a clean kitchen towel. Twist and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Return to bowl.
Mix flour, salt, and Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning in a small bowl. Add egg product and mix; stir into zucchini and onion mixture. Form 4 patties.
Heat oil over high heat in a large nonstick frying pan. Lower heat to medium and place zucchini patties into pan. Sauté until brown, turning once.
hints: Serve with 1 tablespoon applesauce or cranberry sauce.

title: Baked Donuts
description: Making homemade donuts is a rewarding experience. DaVita dietitian Robin’s Baked Donuts recipe includes a protein boost plus whole wheat flour to increase fiber.
steps: Preheat oven to 425° F. Lightly grease 2 standard donut pans (12 donuts)
Using an electric mixer, in a medium bowl, beat together 4 tablespoons butter, oil and granulated and brown sugars until smooth.
Add the eggs, mixing them to combine.
Stir in baking powder, baking soda, nutmeg, salt and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Stir the flour and protein powder into the butter mixture alternately with the yogurt and milk. Start and end with the flour mixture. Make sure everything is thoroughly combined. The batter will
be fairly thick. When you pull a spatula through your batter, it should leave an indentation.
Spoon the batter into the lightly greased donut pans, filling to about 1/4-inch from the top. Alternatively, you can pipe the batter into the donut pan using a piping bag.
Bake the donuts for 10 minutes. Remove pans from the oven, and allow donuts to cool for 5 to 7 minutes. Remove donuts from the pan and allow to cool completely.
While the donuts are cooling, make the glaze. Stir sifted confectioner’s sugar, corn syrup, remaining vanilla, butter (melted) and 1 tablespoon milk together in a shallow bowl. Add extra milk or
confectioner’s sugar as needed to adjust consistency.
Pour sprinkles in a separate shallow bowl.
Dip top of donut in glaze to coat, then dip in sprinkles. Place on rack to set.
hints: You can also bake batter in mini muffin tins, then glaze and add sprinkles to make “donut holes”.
If whole wheat pastry flour is unavailable substitute 1 cup whole wheat flour and 1 cup all-purpose flour (in addition to the 2/3 cup all-purpose flour).
This recipes is high in protein and fiber and lower in sodium compared to bakery donuts.

title: Caraway Rye Bread
description: There’s an art to baking yeast bread. Bring out your inner artist with DaVita dietitian Tara’s Caraway Rye Bread recipe. It’s low in sodium and high in flavor!
steps: In a stand mixer, combine flour, salt, yeast and caraway seeds.
Make a well in the center of flour mixture and add warm water.
Mix until dough becomes wet and sticky.
Cover with plastic wrap and sit in warm, dry place for 3 hours.
Heat the oven to 450° F. Place an enamel Dutch oven with the lid on in the oven. Allow to heat for 30 minutes.
While the Dutch oven is heating, scrape the dough out of the bowl and place onto a floured board or counter top.
Flour your hands and fold the dough over a few times; making a ball with the dough. Make the seam at the bottom of the dough.
Carefully remove Dutch oven from the oven and place dough inside. Replace the lid and return to oven. Cook for 30 minutes or until internal temperature of the bread reaches 200° F.
Remove from oven and transfer to a cooling rack. Cut cooled bread into 16 pieces.
hints: For a crustier crust, can cook for an additional 10 minutes with cover of Dutch oven removed.
This recipe works best in a Dutch oven. Loaf pan not recommended.

title: Zesty Cucumber Salad
description: This simple kidney-friendly recipe is bursting with flavor from cucumbers, Italian dressing and red onion. That’s why Zesty Cucumber Salad will make an appearance at the dinner table more than once.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Kraft® Light Done Right!® Italian salad dressing
steps: Peel and seed cucumbers; slice onion.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes to marinate.
Serve chilled.
hints: Decrease carbohydrate to 4 grams by using sugar substitute instead of sugar.
Leftovers will keep in the refrigerator up to one week.

title: Basil Pesto
description: Enjoy a serving of vegetables blended into this Basil Pesto. It’s a great addition to pasta or as a marinade or topping on seafood or chicken. This creative recipe replaces the cheese with nutritional yeast.
steps: Juice the lemon. Add all ingredients except flax and olive oils to a food processor.
Combine the oils and pour oil into the food processor through the top to evenly emulsify while blending the ingredients. Stir ingredients from the bottom of the blender as needed.
Store pesto in a jar or covered container until ready to use as a marinade, salad dressing or pasta sauce. Keeps up to one week in the refrigerator.
hints: An additional 2 tablespoons of flax oil may be substituted for the olive oil.
Flax oil provides health benefits including supplying ALA omega-3 fatty acids.

Basil Pesto has great versatility- use as a marinade on seafood or chicken, as a dipping sauce for fresh or roasted vegetables, a salad dressing or toss with pasta or rice as a lower potassium alternative to tomato sauce.

title: Curry Sauce with Chicken
description: Karen, a DaVita renal dietitian from California, spices up the kidney diet with a hearty Curry Sauce that can be paired with seafood, chicken or beef. Sugar-free and made with low-sodium broth, this sauce is perfect for people managing kidney disease. Karen’s Curry Sauce is versatile, kidney-friendly and a great way to add some heat to meat.
steps: Mince garlic and ginger. Finely chop carrots, celery, and onion. Slice mushrooms. Chop apple.
Combine flour, garlic, ginger, curry powder and vegetable oil in a non-stick, deep skillet (at least 4 quarts) over a medium heat.
Stir until curry becomes paste-like.
Slowly add broth, and stir until sauce is smooth.
Add vegetables, apple and white pepper.
Simmer, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes, or until well blended.
Bring sauce to a boil and add chicken.
Simmer curry for 1-1/2 hours over a low heat, stirring regularly and serve.
hints: Save time by using Trader Joe’s® Mirepoix mix, a pre-chopped, pre-washed container of carrots, celery and onion.
Substitute beef or seafood for chicken for variety. If using raw beef, brown it before adding to curry in step 6.
For CKD non-dialysis on a lower protein diet, decrease portion to 3/4 cup.
Serve over rice for a complete meal.

title: Pineapple Angel Cake
description: The delightfully refreshing flavor of pineapple combines with light angel food cake in this kidney-friendly recipe for Pineapple Angel Cake. DaVita renal dietitian, Kim from Kentucky, says her easy-to-make recipe makes a yummy dessert or snack.
ingredients: 20 ounces canned crushed pineapple, juice pack
8 ounces Cool Whip® frozen dessert topping, thawed
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Blend dry cake mix and entire can of undrained pineapple with a mixer until well blended and fluffy.
Pour mixture into an ungreased 9″ x 13″ cake pan. Bake 25 to 30 minutes until lightly brown on top.
Cool completely.
Frost with non-dairy whipped topping. Store in the refrigerator.
hints: For higher calories use pineapple packed in heavy syrup.

title: Overnight Oats with Pears and Spice
description: Minimum preparation required wit Karol’s Pumpkin Pie Spice Oats with Pears. Mix ingredients in a jar, refrigerate overnight, then enjoy for a quick breakfast.
steps: Dice the pear half.
Combine all ingredients in a mason jar and stir well. Refrigerate overnight.
Ready to eat the next day. You can take your breakfast on-the-go. Heating is not necessary. Add sweetener if desired.
hints: Prepare a few jars at a time for quick breakfasts all week.

If you desire a crunchy texture use fresh pears and add them in the morning. Instead of fresh pears you can substitute a fruit cup of diced pears (drained) or other low potassium fruits such as apple, berries, cherries or peach.
The soaking of the oats overnight acts as “cooking”. If warm oatmeal is preferred microwave the jar for 1-2 minutes before eating.

title: Broiled Honey Grapefruit
description: When you’re on a kidney diet, this recipe for Broiled Honey Grapefruit is a delicious and healthy way to start your morning.
steps: Preheat broiler to 400º F.
Cut grapefruit in half then cut around the edges and sections of each grapefruit half.
Drizzle the top of each half with a teaspoon of honey and 1/8 teaspoon cinnamon.
Broil grapefruit for 6 minutes or until it starts to brown.
Serve hot.
hints: Sectioning the grapefruit before broiling makes it easier to eat.
Grapefruit and grapefruit juice are known to interact with some medications. Check with your healthcare team to be sure grapefruit is safe to include in your diet.

title: Roasted Summer Vegetables
description: Roasted vegetables caramelize on the outside while remaining tender on the inside—with natural flavor that requires no added salt. Try Tammi’s Roasted Summer Vegetable recipe for the right mix or lower potassium vegetables.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Rinse and dry vegetables. Cut turnips and carrot into 2-inch pieces; mince garlic.
Place turnips, carrots and half of the minced garlic in a bowl and drizzle with 2 teaspoons of olive oil. Add marjoram and toss to coat vegetables with oil.
Spray two baking sheets with nonstick cooking spray; divide and layer vegetables evenly on sheets. Place baking sheets in oven for 30 minutes.

While turnips and carrots are cooking, cut onion, red bell pepper and zucchini into 2-inch pieces and slice mushrooms in half. Remove ends from green beans but keep them whole. Place vegetables in a bowl and drizzle with 2 teaspoons of olive oil. Add remaining garlic and black pepper; toss gently until vegetables are coated with oil.

After turnips and carrots have cooked for 30 minutes remove baking sheets from oven. Divide the green bean vegetable mixture between the two baking sheets. Mix vegetables with partially cooked turnips and carrots, forming a single layer on the baking sheets. Return to oven for another 15–20 minutes, cooking until vegetables are tender.
hints: Roasted vegetables have extra flavor compared to steamed or boiled vegetables. No salt is needed.
Experiment with different vegetable combinations.

title: Savory Green Beans
description: Enjoy the delectable and kidney-friendly recipe for Savory Green Beans.
ingredients: 1 pound frozen French style green beans
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Chop onion and mince garlic.
Cook green beans in microwave according to package directions.
In a medium skillet, heat oil and sauté onion with garlic, until onion is translucent.
Add dill weed, lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce and stir to mix.
Add green beans and toss. Place in a casserole dish.
Melt butter and mix with bread crumbs. Sprinkle over green bean mixture and bake for 5 to 10 minutes to brown.

title: Red Wine Vinaigrette Asparagus
description: Enjoy this kidney-friendly recipe for Red Wine Vinaigrette Asparagus at your next weekend dinner.
steps: Mince the garlic; cut the asparagus into 2″ pieces.
Heat the oil in a skillet, add the garlic and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the asparagus pieces; stir to mix.
Add the red wine vinaigrette dressing and pepper.
Stir and heat an additional minute.
Remove from the heat and serve.
hints: Make your own red wine vinaigrette dressing by combining equal parts of red wine vinegar and olive oil with low sodium herb blend.

title: Lemonade Rice with Mixed Vegetbles
description: Lemonade Rice with Mixed Vegetables is a delicious and easy-to-make kidney-friendly recipe.
steps: Mince onion.
Pour lemonade and water into rice cooker or saucepan. Add rice, onion, mixed vegetables and seasonings.
Start rice cooker or cook on stove, covered, over medium heat for 20 minutes.
hints: Fresh, frozen, bottled or canned lemonade may be used in this recipe. Be aware, some lemonades contain phosphate additives which increases phosphorus content. Read labels and avoid brands with this additive.
Select a vegetable mix with carrots, corn, green beans, green peas or substitute your favorite low potassium frozen vegetable blend.
If you have diabetes, try sugar-free lemonade in this recipe to lower carbohydrates by 5 grams per serving.
For best results, do not remove cover or stir rice during cooking.

title: Mixed Vegetable Salad
description: Red pepper, lemon juice and cucumber are just a few of the yummy ingredients that make up the kidney-friendly recipe, Mixed Vegetable Salad.
steps: Peel, seed and dice cucumber and red pepper.
Chop dill and scallions.
Combine all ingredients in a serving bowl and mix.
Chill for at least one hour before serving.
hints: Use low-fat sour cream if desired.

title: Grand Champion Apple Pie
description: Grand Champion Apple Pie was submitted by renal dietitian Barb from North Carolina. Bake up this kidney-friendly deep-dish delight and enjoy the pleasing aromas as well as the tantalizing flavors.
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
In a large mixing bowl, combine eggs, applesauce, brown sugar, flour, lemon rind, 3-tablespoons lemon juice, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg; mix well.

Pour mixture into unbaked pie shell. Bake for 15 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 300° F. Bake for 45 minutes longer or until knife inserted near center comes out clean. Cool slightly on wire rack.
While pie is baking, peel and thinly slice apple.
Combine apple slices and 1 tablespoon lemon juice in a bowl; mix well. Arrange apple slices pinwheel fashion over top of baked pie.
Melt jam in small saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly. Brush apple slices with melted jam.
Place pie on rack of broiler pan. Broil 6” from heat source for 3 minutes or until apples are tender and jam is bubbly.
hints: Lower carbohydrate options for diabetics include using 1/4 cup + 2 tablespoons Splenda® Brown Sugar Blend instead of brown sugar, and using apricot fruit spread instead of jam. This reduces calories to 216, carbohydrate 32 g and 2 carbohydrate choices.
Sodium content of pre-made pie crust varies with brands. Select the brand with lowest sodium content or consider making homemade pie crust with reduced salt.

title: Rice and Chile Salad with Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing
description: Add a hint of spice to the kitchen table with this kidney-friendly recipe, Rice and Chile Salad with Creamy Vinaigrette Dressing.
ingredients: 1 cup long grain white rice, uncooked
steps: To cook rice, bring 1-3/4 cups water to a boil in a 2-quart saucepan and add rice and salt. Bring water to a boil again, stir once, cover and reduce heat to simmer for 15 minutes or until water has evaporated. Remove from heat and set, covered for at least 10 minutes.

To roast chile, place under broiler, turning often until uniformly charred. When the pepper is blackened on all sides, transfer to a plastic bag or bowl, cover and seal and let cool. Remove charred skin from chiles, rinse and pat dry. Dice the chilies.
Thaw peas; peel and seed cucumber; chop cucumber,green onions and cilantro; dice bell peppers and mince garlic.
To assemble salad, combine rice and diced chiles. Add thawed peas, bell peppers, onion, cucumber and cilantro. Toss well to combine.
To prepare dressing, combine all dressing ingredients and mix well.
Toss dressing with rice and vegetable mixture. Chill until ready to serve.
hints: Poblano chiles are also known as ancho chiles.
Roast chiles ahead of time to allow time to cool.
Wear rubber gloves when removing seeds and vein from hot chiles.
For a nice presentation, serve on a platter lined with lettuce leaves.

title: Turkey Stuffed Green Peppers
description: Try this kidney-friendly recipe for Turkey Stuffed Green Peppers at your next dinner.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Remove stems from peppers and clean seeds and membranes from inside.
Mix turkey, rice, egg, onion, garlic and seasonings well.
Stuff peppers with meat mixture.
Place peppers in a large roaster.
Pour crushed tomatoes and broth over peppers
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes.
hints: Use ground turkey breast for the leanest possible filling, but lean ground beef is also a heart-healthy filling.
If you are not on a potassium restricted diet, use a 16-oz. can of crushed tomatoes.
Make a double batch and freeze individual peppers for an easy meal when you don’t feel like cooking.

Stuffed peppers are ubiquitous throughout Central and Eastern Europe. Seasoning and what type of meat with which they are stuffed vary not only from region to region, but within regions. Some use 100% ground beef, and others use a mixture of meats.
For a lower protein diet you can use one pound of turkey and increase the rice to 3 cups.

title: Watermelon Agua Fresca
description: Fresh water blended with watermelon and lime juice is a perfect thirst quencher for a hot summer day or anytime. Watermelon Agua Fresca is low in potassium making it a great choice for a kidney diet.
steps: Cut the lime into slices. Cut the watermelon into large chunks and measure 2 cups.
Place the watermelon in a blender along with 2 lime slices and blend until smooth.
Use a sieve to strain the mixture and pour into 4 cups. Garnish with mint leaves and lime slices and serve.
hints: Replace sugar with stevia sweetener to reduce carbohydrates to 12 grams.

title: Pineapple Non-Dairy “Ice Cream” Treats
description: Only four ingredients and no cooking required makes Pineapple Non-Dairy "ice Cream" treats budget-friendly and easy to make.
ingredients: 20 ounce can crushed pineapple, well drained
steps: Mix drained pineapple and protein powder well, fold in the whipped topping.
Place a single layer of graham cracker squares on a cookie sheet and spread about 2 tablespoons topping mixture on each cracker.
Place another graham cracker square on top and place cookie sheet in the freezer.
When well frozen, wrap individually in plastic wrap and store them in an airtight container in the freezer.
hints: Some whipped toppings have phosphorus additives. Look at the ingredients list to be sure phosphorus is not added.
A 14.4 ounce box of graham crackers contains about 27 rectangle sheets.
Protein powder can vary in protein, potassium, phosphorus and sodium. You may talk to your dietitian to see which one would be appropriate for you.

title: Green Beans a la Roast
description: Never before have you tasted veggies like these! DaVita renal dietitian Brady from Ohio shows us how to roast green beans so they’re tender and tantalizing! With this dish, you won’t have to worry about getting your kids to eat their vegetables. And it also fits into a kidney-friendly diet so you can be sure that everyone will be asking for seconds of Green Beans a la Roast!
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
Wash green beans and trim ends.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil and spread beans on foil.
Pour olive oil over beans and toss gently to coat beans evenly.
Roast in oven for 10 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from oven and redistribute beans for even baking.
Return to oven and bake for approximately 10 additional minutes or until beans have a few golden brown areas.
Remove from oven, season with ground pepper and serve.
hints: For extra flavor try a flavored oil with llemon or herb flavor.

title: Coconut Bread
description: Shredded coconut and sour cream give kidney-friendly Coconut Bread the perfect balance of sweetness and moistness. Add some pineapple to turn it into a Hawaiian treat.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. Set butter out to soften.
Warm coconut oil in microwave until just melted. Set aside to cool.
Cream butter and sugar together. Add coconut oil and eggs; stir together. Mix in sour cream. Add shredded coconut to mixture and stir.
In a separate bowl mix together flour, baking soda and baking powder.
Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients. Pour batter into the loaf pan.
Bake 45 to 60 minutes, until bread is golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool bread in pan for 5 to 10 minutes then remove from pan and cool on a wire rack.
hints: If desired add 1/2 cup of diced or crushed pineapple.
Wrap some of the bread slices in freezer wrap and freeze for a quick snack later.

title: Poached Pears
description: Ready to transformplain pears into a tasty dessert? DaVita renal dietitian, Geri from Washington will show you how to make delicious foods for the kidney diet with her kidney-friendly recipe for Poached Pears.
steps: Mix cinnamon and sugar in a small bowl.
Cut pears in half and using a spoon scoop out seeds and stem.
Make a thin slice across round part of pear, so that it lays flat in baking dish.
Place pears skin side down in a baking dish and sprinkle tops with cinnamon and sugar mix.
Place 1 teaspoon butter in the seed hole of each pear.
Pour juice in bottom of pan.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° F approximately 30 minutes or until pear is soft when poked with fork.
hints: If your baking dish is shallow you may need less juice. The juice should only come halfway up the side of the pears.
Pour juice over pears before serving if desired.
For people with diabetes use low calorie cranberry juice and subar substitute instead of sugar.

title: Asparagus Cauliflower Tortilla
description: Cindy, a DaVita renal dietitian from Wisconsin, focuses on her patient’s individual kidney dietary wishes and tries to make them a reality. A delicious, dialysis diet recipe such as her tasty and filling Asparagus Cauliflower Tortilla is simple to prepare and will satisfy your hunger, keep your taste buds happy and help make your dreams of healthy lab results come true.
ingredients: 2 cups asparagus, chopped in bite size pieces
2 cups cauliflower, chopped in bite size pieces
1 cup liquid low cholesterol egg substitute
steps: Place asparagus and cauliflower pieces plus 1 tablespoon water in a microwave-proof, covered dish. Microwave for 3 to 5 minutes to steam until tender crisp.
Sauté the onion until golden, about 7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, 1 minute longer.
Stir in the asparagus, cauliflower, egg substitute, parsley, salt, pepper, thyme and nutmeg.
Reduce heat and cook covered until set and browned on bottom, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Loosen the edges with a knife and invert onto a warm platter or serve directly from skillet.
hints: In Spain and South America, a tortilla is a round, unfolded omelet typically made with eggs, vegetables and seasonings. In comparison, the Mexican tortilla is thin, flat bread made from wheat flour or ground corn.

title: Roasted Cauliflower with Rosemary
description: Cauliflower could easily become your favorite low potassium vegetable after tasting Roasted Cauliflower with Rosemary. Created by the DaVita dietitian team, this veggie roast is lightly seasoned with oil, a small amount of salt, pepper and fresh rosemary. Roasted Cauliflower with Rosemary is easy to make and kidney-friendly.
steps: Preheat oven to 450° F.
Cut cauliflower florets into bite-size pieces. Chop rosemary.
In a large bowl, toss cauliflower with remaining ingredients.
Spread seasoned cauliflower on an ungreased baking sheet.
Roast for 15 minutes; remove from oven and stir.
Continue roasting for 10 minutes or until cauliflower is tender and lightly browned.
hints: Use caution when removing baking sheet from oven to stir cauliflower.

title: Italian Style Vegetables & Pasta with Chicken
description: Try the kidney-friendly recipe for Italian Style Vegetables & Pasta with Chicken for your next big dinner.
steps: Chop bell pepper and onion. Dice chicken.
Place oil in a large nonstick frying pan and stir-fry the bell pepper, onion and broccoli. Sprinkle with the rosemary, basil, red pepper flakes, garlic powder and salt.
Stir in the cooked chicken.
Mix chicken broth with cornstarch and add to vegetable and chicken mixture. Cook until thickened slightly. Stir in the cup of hot cooked pasta.
Remove from heat and serve.
hints: Chicken may be increased to 6 ounces for those on dialysis. Protein content will be increased to 29 grams per serving.
For quick preparation, use 1-1/4 cups of a frozen vegetable mixture of similar composition to replace fresh vegetables.
Add more or less red pepper flakes to suit your own tolerance for spicy foods.
Squeeze on lemon juice or sprinkle with balsamic vinegar to add a tangy flavor.

title: Ground Beef and Veggie Foil Pack Dinner
description: Easy to assemble and easy to clean up is a perfect description for DaVita dietitian Graces’ recipe, Ground Beef and Veggie Foil Pack Dinner. Plus you can vary the type of protein and veggies to make this recipe an easy go-to kidney-friendly dinner.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Spray a piece of foil with nonstick cooking spray. Chop the onion.
Combine the ground beef, onion and Worcestershire sauce into a patty and place on the foil.
Top patty with frozen peas and carrots.
Sprinkle Italian dressing mix and black pepper over the top.
Fold and seal the foil and place on a baking sheet. Bake for 35 minutes.
Carefully open one end of the foil packet and allow steam to escape before serving.
hints: Spray the foil with cooking spray.
Place the foil packet on a baking sheet before placing in the oven.

title: Hazelnut Cinnamon Coffee
description: Start the day off on a delicious note with the kidney-friendly recipe for Hazelnut Cinnamon Coffee.
ingredients: 8 teaspoons Torani® Sugar Free Classic Hazelnut Syrup
steps: Brew coffee in coffee maker. Pour into small cups.
Add 2 teaspoons of the Torani® Sugar Free Classic Hazelnut Syrup and 1 tablespoon of milk (or creamer) to each mug and garnish each with a cinnamon stick.
hints: Try different flavors of the Torani® Sugar Free syrups.
If you prefer your coffee darker, omit the milk.
Many nondairy creamers contain phosphate additives. Be aware if you substitute nondairy hazelnut creamer for the syrup.

title: Cinnamon Roll Cake
description: Ingredients Preparation Helpful hints
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Melt 1/2 cup butter and leave remaining butter out to soften.
In medium-sized bowl, mix 3 cups flour, salt, 1 cup Splenda baking blend, baking soda, cream of tartar, 1-1/2 cups Rice Dream, eggs and 2 teaspoons vanilla. Slowly stir in melted butter.
Pour mixture into a greased 9″ x 13″ pan.
Mix 1 cup softened butter, Splenda brown sugar blend, 2 tablespoons flour and cinnamon until well combined. Drop evenly over the batter and swirl with a knife.
Bake for 28-32 minutes.
Combine remaining 1 cup Splenda baking blend and powdered sugar, 5 tablespoons rice milk and 1 teaspoon vanilla. Drizzle over cake while it’s still warm.
hints: This high calorie dessert is great for boosting calories. Enjoy for breakfast or dessert.
If available,1 cup Ideal® powdered sugar substitute may be used to replace 1 cup Splenda baking blend and 1 cup powdered sugar to reduce calories and carbohydrates.

title: Turkey Meatloaf
description: Sara’s kidney-friendly recipe for Turkey Meatloaf features a bit of hot turkey sausage, providing a kick you don’t expect but will really enjoy.Turkey Meatloaf may look familiar, but will introduce you to a whole new flavor.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Gravy Master® seasoning & browning sauce
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl and mix well.
Transfer to a greased 9″ x 5″ loaf pan and bake for 1 hour.
Slice into 6 equal pieces and serve.
hints: Select the brand of sausage lowest in sodium.
Use the hot and spicy turkey sausage for more flavor.

title: Pomegranate Refresher
description: Pomegranate juice, lemon juice and club soda are combined to create this festive, sparkling Pomegranate Refresher.
steps: Add pomegranate and lemon juice to a small glass.
Top with club soda.
Add in pomegranate arils and garnish with lemon.
hints: Pomegranate juice is limited to 1/4 cup in this recipe. One cup of pomegranate juice contains over 500 mg potassium.
Substitute cranberry juice for pomegranate juice if preferred. Potassium is decreased to 46 mg.
Add a small amount of your favorite sweetener for added sweetness.

title: Lamb or Mutton Stew with Dumplings
description: If you’ve never tried it, or don’t serve it often, DaVita renal dietitian, Miriam from Arizona, has a Lamb or Mutton Stew with Dumplings recipe that is tasty, renal-friendly and a one-dish meal that cooks everything in a single pot.
steps: Measure water and put in a stew pot.
Trim fat from meat and cut into bite-size pieces. Add meat and bones to water. Set on stove over medium heat.
Coarsely chop onion. Cut zucchini in half lengthwise and sliced into 1/2” slices
Add onion, zucchini and chilies to stew.
Once the stew has come to a low boil, turn heat to low and let simmer for at least 1 hour.
While stew is cooking, mix flour, salt, baking powder and sugar in a bowl.
Knead in warm water to dry ingredients to form a soft ball of dough.
Cover dough and let it rest for 20 to 30 minutes.
After cooking stew for 1 hour, shape an approximately 2-1/2” dough ball into a flat round. (It does not need to be perfect or flat).
Tear off penny-sized pieces of dough and drop them into the stew.
Continue to shape 2-1/2” dough ball into a flat round and tear off penny-sized pieces of dough and drop in stew until all dough is in stew.
Cook dumplings in the stew for an additional 20 minutes.
Serve and enjoy.
hints: Roast 2-3 Hatch chilies instead of canned chilies.

title: Shake and Bake Chicken Extravaganza
description: Patience isn’t just a virtue, it’s a talent. Just like cooking, developing compassion is a skill that can be perfected, as Mary, a DaVita renal dietitian from Minnesota has demonstrated. Mary has honed her skill for “patience with patients,” as well as, her inventiveness for creating delicious recipes, such as her kidney-friendly Shake and Bake Chicken Extravaganza.
serving_size: 1 piece of chicken (3 ounces without bone)
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Grease baking sheet with vegetable oil (can use parchment paper or silpat sheet) and set aside.
Combine bread crumbs, flour, parsley, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, marjoram and thyme. Stir to mix evenly.
Add oil to bread crumb mixture and stir with a fork to blend completely.
Store in airtight container in cool, dry place or store in freezer.
To prepare chicken: Rinse chicken with water and leave chicken pieces moist with water while shaking off excess liquid.
Pour 1 cup of bread crumb mixture into a clean plastic food storage bag. Add 1 to 2 pieces of chicken at a time to bag and shake to coat evenly.
Place on greased baking sheet and bake for 40 to 45 minutes. Turn once, after 20 minutes.
hints: This recipe makes enough coating mix for 3 meals. Store the remaining mixture in a sealed container or freezer bag and freeze until ready to use again.
To homemade dry breadcrumbs, toast day old bread until crisp but not burned. Crush in a blender or food processor.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Carrots and Apples
description: Enhance the flavor of fall vegetables by roasting and adding a hint of maple syrup. Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Carrots and Apples is a kidney-friendly recipe, easy for any dinner and special enough to serve at special dinners.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Spray a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Trim the Brussels sprouts and cut each one in half. Peel the carrots and cut into 1-inch pieces. Core the apple and cut into 1/2-inch cubes.
Place Brussels sprouts, carrots and apple pieces in a large bowl.
In a small bowl combine the olive oil, maple syrup and spices. Stir to combine.
Pour sauce into the large bowl and stir to coat vegetables and apples. Place ingredients on the baking sheet. Sprinkle with the 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until carrots are fork tender and Brussels sprouts begin to darken.
hints: Replace carrots with 2 medium turnips if desired.
Add leftovers to mixed salad greens for a hearty roasted veggie salad the next day.

title: Shrimp Boulettes
description: Shrimp Boulettes are a seafood lovers delight because crab or crawfish can easily be substituted for shrimp. Created by DaVita patient Ken in Louisiana, Shrimp Boulettes give a kidney-friendly twist to an old-time Cajun favorite.
ingredients: 1/2 cup to 1 cup all-purpose white flour
steps: Finely chop shrimp, onion, bell pepper and parsley. Beat eggs.
Mix all of the ingredients except flour together in a mixing bowl.
After mixing, gradually add flour. Continue adding flour a little at a time until mix gets thick and hangs on to the spoon.
To deep fry, heat oil in a large skillet or deep-fryer. Drop medium-sized spoonfuls of shrimp batter into hot oil and cook until browned and crisp on both sides.
Remove from oil and drain on paper towels. Serve hot.
hints: Suggested Cajun seasonings include homemade Salt-free Cajun Seasoning on DaVita.com, Mrs. Dash Cajun seasoning blend or Benoit’s Best Salt-Free Cajun seasoning. Avoid products with potassium chloride.
Instead of frying you can form batter into patties and bake on a greased baking sheet at 350° F until golden brown.
Try crab or crawfish instead of shrimp. Both are equally great!

title: Berries Napoleon
description: Indulge your sweet tooth on the renal diet with Berries Napoleon, a simple, delicious dessert from renal dietitian Marie from Colorado. On its own or paired with an elegant meal, this low potassium dessert is perfect for the kidney diet.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F.
Spray the cooking spray on a baking sheet that will fit 12 wonton wrappers.
Spread out the wonton wrappers, and spray them with cooking spray.
Sprinkle the granulated sugar on wonton wrappers.
Bake the wontons for 5 minutes or until golden brown;remove from the baking sheet.
Place 6 wonton wrappers on a serving tray.
Top each wrapper with 2 tablespoons of whipped topping, 1 tablespoon of raspberries and 1 tablespoon of blueberries.
Top the berries with a second wonton wrapper.
Sprinkle the tops with powdered sugar. Garnish them with a dollop of whipped topping, fruit and a mint leaf, if desired. Serve immediately.
hints: Substitute strawberries and blackberries for raspberries and blueberries for variety.
To reduce carbohydrate content substitute Splenda® No Calorie granular sweetener for sugar.
If the wontons sit in the refrigerator the Reddi-Wip will melt. Assemble only when ready to serve.

title: Poppy Krunch
description: Looking for a quick snack that is light, crunchy and sweet? DaVita renal dietitian Jackie from North Carolina has the answer: Poppy Krunch. Kids will love this treat made from popcorn that’s been drizzled with a buttery-sweet topping, but adults will want their fair share too. And since it’s kidney-friendly, those with renal problems are able to indulge without
steps: Spread popcorn in a shallow pan.
Combine sugar, corn syrup and butter in a 1/2-quart saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until a small amount dropped in cold water separates into thin threads which are hard but not brittle (280° F on the candy thermometer). Remove from heat.
Add vanilla.
Pour syrup over popcorn, stirring until well-coated. Spread on a greased baking sheet. Break into pieces.
Allow to cool. Store in an air tight container until ready to serve.
hints: Portion into individual servings and store for a quick snack or dessert during the week.

title: Easy Turkey Sloppy Joes
description: Enjoy a savory, family favorite that celebrates the Americana diner of yesteryear. DaVita renal dietitian, Tammy from Louisiana, shares a kidney-friendly recipe for Easy Turkey Sloppy Joes.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash® Chicken Grilling Blend seasoning
steps: Chop onion and bell pepper.
Place in a large skillet with turkey and cook over medium high heat until turkey is cooked through. Do not drain.
In a small bowl, mix together the Mrs. Dash® seasoning, sugar, Worcestershire sauce and tomato sauce.
Add seasonings to the turkey mixture. Reduce heat to simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Divide into 6 portions and serve on hamburger buns.
hints: Lean ground beef may be substituted for ground turkey. Drain the fat after browning the beef in preparation step one.
To save time, use frozen chopped onions and bell pepper.
For a lower-protein diet, reduce turkey to 1 pound or portion can be adjusted according to your diet plan.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Baked Apples
description: For your next dessert craving, try the kidney-friendly recipe for Slow Cooker Honey Baked Apples. Our recipe for Slow Cooker Honey Baked Apples was created exclusively for DaVita.com by DaVita renal dietitian Sara from California. This modern, kidney-friendly take on classic baked apples is perfect for those following diabetes, dialysis and CKD non-dialysis diets.
steps: Core and cut each apple into 8 pieces and place in a slow cooker.
Sprinkle cinnamon over apple pieces and toss to coat.
Drizzle with honey, add butter and stir.
Set slow cooker to low temperature, cover with a lid and cook for 2 hours.
hints: This recipe can also be prepared in the oven. Cook at 325° F for 45 to 60 minutes.

title: German Apple Cake
description: German Apple Cake is a combination of sweet apples sliced and stirred into a sweet lemony-cinnamon batter which is then baked until golden brown. This kidney-friendly cake is so tasty that no icing is needed.
steps: Preheat the oven to 325° F. Grease a 9 x 13-inch baking dish. Set butter out to soften. Peel, core and slice apples.

Using a mixer, cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Zest the lemon. Add the lemon zest and vanilla extract to butter and sugar mixture. Add one egg and continue to mix; add the other egg and mix.
In a separate bowl combine the flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed butter until combined. Do not over mix.
Juice the lemon; stir the juice into the batter. Stir in the apple slices.

Pour the batter into the greased baking dish. Sprinkle one tablespoon of sugar over the top. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes. The cake is done when a toothpick inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean. After cake is cool cut into 15 pieces and serve.
hints: Use apple variety of choice.
Cut the cake into 20 pieces for a lower carbohydrate serving (23 grams).

title: Super Fruit Smoothie
description: Marlene, a DaVita dietitian from Florida, says she looks after her patients like a “mother hen.” And, like most moms, she likes to provide good-for-you treats. Marlene’s Super Fruit Smoothie is a perfect, kidney-friendly treat.
ingredients: 8 ounces Vanilla Nepro® with Carb Steady™, chilled
1 cup of frozen peaches or mixed berries
steps: Add frozen fruit to blender.
Add chilled Nepro®, whey protein and crushed ice (if desired).
Blend until smooth.
Pour into glass and serve with straw.
hints: Freeze or refrigerate the leftover portion for later.
Recipe analysis used values for Beneprotein® whey protein powder, 7 gram size scoops. Nutrient values may vary slightly with similar products.

title: Gingerbread Muffins
description: These gingerbread muffins are sure to be a holiday favorite for years to come. Spicy ginger combined with cinnamon and brown sugar come together to create a scrumptious kidney-friendly muffin that’s great for breakfast, dessert or snack.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F. Grease a 12-cup muffin pan or line with paper liners.
In a medium bowl lightly beat the eggs. Beat in the milk, oil, brown sugar and corn syrup.

In a large bowl stir together the flour, baking powder, ginger, and cinnamon. Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the liquid ingredients. Stir gently until just combined: do not over mix.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin pan. Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes, until golden brown and firm to the touch.
Remove from oven and let the muffins cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Serve warm with butter or cream cheese.
hints: Freeze leftover muffins for a quick snack later. Reheat in microwave for 30-45 seconds.
Muffins contain baking powder that contributes to phosphorus content. Ask your dietitian if you need to take a phosphate binder when muffins are eaten as a snack.

title: Broccoli-Onion Latkes (Pancakes)
description: Renal dietitian Marjorie from Arizona shares the kidney-friendly recipe for Broccoli-Onion Latkes (pancakes) that use onion and broccoli as alternatives to potatoes for low-potassium latkes that can be enjoyed by anyone, even those on renal-friendly diets.
steps: Dice broccoli and chop onion.
Boil the diced broccoli in a small amount of water for 5 minutes; drain.
Break eggs into a medium bowl and beat. Add the flour and mix well.
Add the broccoli and onion and stir into the flour/egg mixture until well mixed.
Add olive oil to a frying pan and heat.
Drop the mixture by spoonfuls into the hot oil, making 4 equal portions (or 8 portions is smaller latkes are desired).
Using a spatula, flatten the latkes and fry until brown on both sides.
Drain on a paper towel to soak up extra oil.
Serve hot.
hints: Potato latkes (pancakes), traditionally served during Hanukkah, contain over 600 mg potassium for a comparable serving unless the potatoes are soaked or boiled to reduce potassium. Broccoli-Onion Latkes are a good low-potassium alternative.
The latkes taste best if eaten immediately.
